subject: Subpoena readiness: audit-artifact packaging & bulk export workflow
messages:
From: Jake Reilly <jake.reilly@harborbank.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@harborbank.com>
Date: Sun, 07 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subpoena: need packaging format + delivery timeline

Hi Vanessa / Ben,

We received a preservation subpoena that requires Harbor Bank to produce a set of audit artifacts for a six-month window (Jan–Jun 2026). Legal asked me to confirm the following from Redwood as soon as possible:

- Supported export formats for audit logs (NDJSON, CSV, Parquet?)
- Whether exports include tamper-evidence metadata (SHA256 checksums, immutable timestamps)
- Typical time to prepare a bulk export (size: ~150M events) and recommended delivery mechanisms (S3, secure FTP, physical seeding)
- Chain-of-custody or manifest you can provide with the package

If you can share a short checklist / sample manifest and an estimate for completion, we can open a formal request via procurement/legal. Attached is Harbor's internal checklist for context.

Thanks,
Jake
Jake Reilly
Senior eDiscovery Analyst
Harbor Bank
Attachment: harbor_subpoena_checklist.pdf

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jake Reilly <jake.reilly@harborbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subpoena: need packaging format + delivery timeline

Jake — thanks for the details and the checklist. Looping in Marcus for the technical export specifics and Laura for the handoff / logistics on SLAs.

High level answers up front:
- Export formats: NDJSON (preferred for event preservation), Parquet for analytics-friendly packages, and CSV for small slices. We will produce a canonical NDJSON export that preserves original fields and timestamps.
- Tamper-evidence: yes — we include per-file SHA256 checksums, signed manifest with generation timestamps, and optional detached timestamp tokens if required.
- Delivery: S3 (pre-signed, restricted bucket) is our standard. If Harbor requires direct transfer we can do SFTP over a dedicated host. We can also ship an encrypted physical drive as a last resort but that adds days.
- Timeline: for ~150M events we estimate 3–4 business days to prepare and validate the package (includes extraction, checksum generation, manifest, and QA).

I attached a compact export spec (rdw-audit-extract-spec.ndjson) and the S3 handoff playbook. Marcus — could you confirm extraction footprint (approx GB size), whether we need redaction runs, and any dev tasks for manifest signing?

Next step: can Harbor confirm required delivery method and whether you want the full event payloads or a redacted variant? Once we have that, I'll create a mutual action plan and proposed delivery date.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Lead | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: rdw-audit-extract-spec.ndjson

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jake Reilly <jake.reilly@harborbank.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subpoena: need packaging format + delivery timeline

Jake / team — technical notes below (I kept each answer short):

- Estimated export size: ~150M events == ~420–520 GB NDJSON (depends on event enrichment). Parquet compresses ~3–4x and will be ~120–170 GB.
- Export path: we generate NDJSON shards (time-windowed), compute SHA256 per shard, and produce a single signed manifest.jsonl that lists file, size, checksum, record ranges, and earliest/latest timestamps.
- Immutable timestamps: we can attach an RFC 3161 timestamp token to the manifest on request; otherwise manifest includes UTC ISO8601 generation times and internal HSM-signed digest.
- Redaction: we support redaction at export time via configured filters. Redaction increases validation time; add ~1 business day for verification per 200M events. If Harbor needs redaction, please supply the fields/patterns.
- Delivery options + security:
  * S3: preferred. We'll upload to a customer-controlled, pre-provisioned bucket or provide a time-bound presigned transfer. We support SSE-KMS with customer key or our managed key.
  * SFTP: supported for smaller packages; we recommend a checksum-enabled rsync-like transfer.
  * Physical: encrypted drive with Tamper Evident seals (adds 3–5 business days).
- Validation run: we run an automated validate_manifest job that verifies checksums and record counts; expected extra time 6–10 hours.

Operational timeline example (no redaction, S3 delivery):
1) Day 0 (request received): lock export window and start job config
2) Day 1–2: extract + shard + compute checksums
3) Day 3: manifest sign + QA + validation run
4) Day 3–4: upload to S3 + generate access tokens + deliver handoff package and COC manifest

I can prepare a sample manifest and a short runbook for on-call handoff. Let me know if Harbor requires per-record hashing or only per-file checksums.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Engineering Manager, Data Platform | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: s3-delivery-playbook.txt

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jake Reilly <jake.reilly@harborbank.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subpoena: need packaging format + delivery timeline

Jake — thanks for the quick heads-up. From a contractual/ops perspective:

- SLA & fees: Standard forensic export work is covered under our enterprise support plan up to 48 hours of engineering time; larger requests (like this) trigger a time-and-materials estimate. I'll prepare a short SOW that covers extraction, validation, and packaging.
- Access control: we'll grant Harbor temporary access tokens scoped to the package. Tokens expire after 7 days unless a longer window is explicitly requested.
- Chain-of-custody: the manifest includes operator IDs (Redwood engineer), generation timestamps, and the signed digest. We will also provide an MD5v2 / SHA256 ledger snapshot for independent verification.

Proposed milestone dates if Harbor confirms S3 and no redaction:
- Confirm request & deliverables by EOD Fri 12 Jun 2026
- Export start Mon 15 Jun 2026
- Handoff by Thu 18 Jun 2026

If Harbor approves these milestones I will issue the SOW and a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Jake Reilly <jake.reilly@harborbank.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subpoena: need packaging format + delivery timeline

Thanks team — that all looks good and is exactly the level of detail Legal wanted. Harbor confirms:
- Delivery method: S3 with Harbor-managed bucket; we will provide KMS key ARN for SSE-KMS.
- No redaction required for this production.
- Please proceed with the proposed milestone dates; Ben, please send the SOW and DocuSign link.

Can we schedule a 30-minute handoff call next week to walk through the manifest fields and access process? Tuesday 16 Jun between 10–12 PT works for our legal/eDiscovery group.

Jake
Jake Reilly
Senior eDiscovery Analyst
Harbor Bank
